explanation: Since a motorcycle's stopping ability depends on reaction time plus braking distance, detecting a hazard too late leaves too little time and distance to brake before reaching it, making late detection genuinely dangerous.

Painted road markings are typically smoother than the surrounding asphalt, so they offer noticeably less grip, especially when wet, and can make a motorcycle's tires skid if braking or leaning is done on them.
Oil, grease, and fluid drips from vehicles accumulate mostly in the center of the lane, so riding there reduces tire traction quite apart from any legal rule about lane position.

On an oil slick a motorcycle needs maximum, evenly distributed traction, so the rider should hold a straight line without braking or accelerating and pull in the clutch to remove drivetrain influence on the wheels until clear.
Braking or swerving on a slippery patch can easily break traction, so the safest technique is to keep the motorcycle upright and moving straight through it without touching the brakes.

Releasing the throttle and brakes and pulling in the clutch removes any accelerating or braking force on the tires, letting the motorcycle coast through the low-traction patch with the best chance of keeping its grip.

This vehicle-dimension diagram labels the rear overhang, the distance the body extends behind the rear axle, and the number keyed to that measurement in the picture is 78, which the question is testing the ability to read.
A dirty headlight lens scatters and blocks light output, so it directly shortens the distance the beam actually illuminates, cutting down the rider's field of vision at night.

How well a motorcyclist scans and reads the road for hazards depends heavily on riding skill and posture, since an alert, well-positioned rider spots developing dangers earlier than one relying only on the bike's mechanical condition.
Israeli traffic regulations require both the rider and any passenger on a motorcycle to wear a crash helmet before a passenger may legally be carried.
Leaning a motorcycle into a turn tilts the tire so a smaller portion of its tread stays flat on the road, shrinking the contact patch and the traction margin available for steering and braking.

Because braking hard while leaned over can easily break traction, the safe technique is to complete most of the slowing down before entering the curve and use only very gentle braking, if any, once turning.
A motorcycle may only carry a passenger if the vehicle's registration document (license) specifically records it as approved for a passenger.
Looking through the turn toward its exit lets the rider naturally steer along the intended path, a standard technique since a motorcycle tends to follow where the eyes are pointed.
Leaning the motorcycle shifts its balance so that the combined weight and centrifugal force line up through the tire contact patch, counteracting the outward centrifugal force generated in the turn.
Leaning the motorcycle into the turn is how a rider counteracts the outward-pulling centrifugal force and keeps the combined forces balanced through the tires.
Crossing a sidewalk is only permitted at the point needed to enter a private yard or garage, not as a general shortcut or for picking up or dropping off passengers.
Braking sharply mid-turn overloads the already-reduced rear tire contact patch caused by the lean angle, which typically breaks traction and slides the rear wheel out.
Straightening the motorcycle as much as possible maximizes the tire's contact patch and grip on a slippery patch, which takes priority even if it means momentarily crossing outside the lane.

Because a motorcycle cannot brake hard and swerve at the same time without risking loss of control, braking must be finished and eased off just before the obstacle so the rider can then steer around it.

Motorcycles should be serviced on the schedule set out in the manufacturer's manual, since that schedule is calibrated to the specific machine rather than to informal judgment or only the annual test.
Traffic regulations set minimum illumination distances for vehicle headlights at night — 100 meters for high beam and 30 meters for low beam — so a driver can see and stop within the lit range.
An effective safety cushion around a motorcycle comes from actively choosing the right lane position and speed for the traffic conditions at hand, not from a fixed position or simply driving fast.
Keeping distance to the front, rear, and sides gives a rider the reaction time and physical space needed to respond safely if a nearby vehicle suddenly creates a hazard.
Israeli law requires a warning triangle to be carried in vehicles including agricultural trailers, so it can be placed on the road if the vehicle breaks down or stops unexpectedly.
The duty to keep a safe distance from surrounding traffic rests on the motorcyclist himself; he cannot rely on other drivers to maintain that space for him.

Closely watching how nearby vehicles are behaving lets a rider spot early warning signs of a developing hazard, which is a more effective defensive measure than matching their speed or accepting less following distance.
A tractor, like other vehicles, may cross a sidewalk only at the point needed to enter a yard or garage, not to pick up or drop off passengers.

A foot brake that isn't working properly is a serious safety defect, so the rider must stop and have it repaired immediately rather than continue riding or try to compensate with tire pressure changes.
Overtaking must be done from the left of the vehicle being passed while keeping an adequate side clearance, which is the standard rule for passing safely rather than crowding the other vehicle.

Because mirrors leave blind spots a motorcyclist can't fully trust, the safe way to rejoin the lane after overtaking is to check the mirrors and then confirm with a quick glance back over the shoulder before moving over.
Riding a motorcycle with the silencer removed from the exhaust is not permitted under any circumstances, since it is a listed vehicle-condition violation regardless of the type of road.

A motorcyclist's ability to spot obstacles in time depends heavily on where the bike is positioned within the lane and relative to surrounding traffic, since that position determines the rider's actual sightlines.

Keeping adequate distance from the vehicle ahead and maintaining a clear, active field of vision are what actually give a rider the time and visibility needed to react to an object falling from that vehicle.
A motorcyclist may only ride briefly onto a sidewalk to cross it while entering adjoining premises, not to travel along it or bypass traffic.
Regulations governing commercial drivers of heavy vehicles require a rest period of at least 25 consecutive hours within every 8-day cycle, to limit fatigue-related risk.
Reading the labeled rear-overhang measurement (the distance the body extends behind the rear axle) in this vehicle's diagram gives a value of 7, which is what the question is testing.

Traffic signal 711 is the directional signal used to indicate that vehicle and tram drivers may proceed only to the right at that point, distinguishing it from the other numbered signals in that series.
Pedestrians sometimes step out between queued cars away from a marked, regulated crossing, and a filtering motorcyclist's limited sightlines between the rows make that a real collision risk.
A driver in a stopped or slow-moving row may suddenly change lanes into the gap a motorcyclist is using to filter through, often without checking mirrors or blind spots for a bike there.
Restrictions noted on a driving license are legally binding conditions the driver must follow, not optional guidance the driver can choose to ignore.
A motorcyclist, like any motor vehicle, is not permitted to ride on a marked pedestrian path, which is reserved for pedestrian safety.
Full head protection along with abrasion-resistant pants, sturdy high shoes, gloves, and a proper riding jacket form the recommended minimum protective gear for safe motorcycle riding.
Israeli traffic law requires every motorcycle, regardless of type, to be fitted with at least one mirror; it is not left to the rider's discretion.

A proper motorcycle helmet must meet the required safety standard, protect the chin as a full-face design does, and fit the rider's head correctly, since strength and fit both matter for real protection.
Continuous braking on a long winding descent overheats the brake components, which reduces friction and produces weaker braking than normal — a phenomenon known as brake fade.
High boots made of abrasion- and friction-resistant material protect the foot and ankle and keep their grip on the footpegs, unlike light shoes or sandals.
Placing luggage close to the motorcycle's center of gravity and as low as possible, without it sticking out front or rear, minimizes its effect on the bike's balance and handling.
On a wet road a motorcycle's tires lose grip more severely the faster it is going, so the risk of skidding and rolling over rises with speed rather than falling.
An ATV may only carry an additional passenger if that is specifically indicated in the vehicle's registration document, the same principle applied to motorcycle passengers.

Changing to tires of a different size than shown in the vehicle's registration document is not allowed unless the Licensing Authority grants prior approval, since it affects the vehicle's approved specifications.

The statutory maximum length for this class of vehicle combination is set by the traffic regulations, and the value shown for it in the picture — 18.75 meters — is the legal limit the question is testing.
Riding in the dark limits how well a rider can judge the road's surface and condition and spot obstacles with enough time to react, which is the core risk of night riding.
Since the headlight is fixed to the motorcycle's body, leaning or turning tilts the beam away from the actual direction of travel, diverting light from exactly where it is needed on the road ahead.
A scratched or dirty visor scatters and breaks up light rays, especially from oncoming headlights at night, which significantly degrades the rider's quality of vision.

Rubber degrades with age regardless of how little a tire has been used, so checking the manufacture date to make sure it isn't older than about six years is essential even when buying what looks like a new tire.
Keeping the visor free of scratches and treating it with anti-fog and water-repellent products stops rain from fogging or beading on it, preserving clear vision while riding.
A passenger should sit astride the proper pillion seat with feet on the footpegs and hold a grab handle or the rider, which keeps them stable and balanced with the motorcycle.
An untrained passenger's movements while mounting, riding, or dismounting can destabilize the motorcycle, so guiding them on how to get on and off and how to sit correctly is the key safety point.
Israeli law specifically bars a Class A2 license holder from carrying a passenger younger than 18 years old.
Coordinated use of both the front and rear brakes together gives a motorcycle its maximum, most controlled stopping power, which is the standard braking technique.
A rider who first obtains an A1 or A2 license as an adult must hold it for at least two months before being legally allowed to carry a passenger.
The correct technique for a road obstacle is to slow down before reaching it rather than braking on top of it, shifting to neutral, or trying to power through without adjusting speed.
A newly licensed tractor driver must wait at least six months from receiving the license before towing a trailer whose total weight exceeds 4,000 kg, a probationary restriction on heavier towing.
A tractor driver may not carry a passenger until at least three months have passed since the tractor driving license was obtained, a similar probationary limit to other new-driver passenger rules.

Before entering any intersection a rider's essential duty is to confirm it is actually clear of traffic that could endanger him, since having the right of way never guarantees another driver will actually yield.
A Class A2 license in Israel is limited to motorcycles with engine power of up to 11 kW (about 14.6 horsepower), a statutory power ceiling for that license category.
Class A motorcycles are subject to the same general speed limits as private cars unless signed otherwise: 50 km/h in urban areas and 80 km/h on inter-urban roads.
Motorcycle mirrors should be adjusted while the bike is standing upright with its handlebar centered in line with the frame, so the setting matches the rider's actual straight-ahead riding position.
Brake pads are manufactured with a visible wear-indicator mark, so a rider can tell they need replacing by that mark rather than waiting until the padding disappears entirely.
Counting the axle sets shown for each numbered semi-trailer in the picture identifies the one built with three axles, which the question is asking the rider to pick out visually.

The vehicle in the picture is identifiable as an articulated vehicle (a tractor unit with a semi-trailer resting on it, rather than a separate towed trailer), a configuration whose statutory maximum overall length is fixed at 17.60 meters by the traffic regulations.
A used tire's rubber can be aged well beyond its visible wear, so checking its manufacture date to confirm it is not older than about two years is the critical check before buying it.

A speeding conviction during the new-driver probation period can lead the Licensing Authority to require a new driving test, and passing it resets the driver to "new driver" status for another two years rather than simply renewing the license.

An illuminated oil-pressure warning light signals that the engine may be running without adequate lubrication and could suffer serious damage, so the driver must stop and shut off the engine immediately rather than continue driving.
A retarder is a supplementary device used to reduce vehicle speed, most notably on a long descent, without relying on or wearing out the vehicle's regular braking system.
Traffic regulations require a driver to signal whenever intending to change driving lanes, so that other road users are warned of the movement in advance.

The general duty of care requires a driver to reduce speed, including coming to a full stop, whenever a hazard is or could reasonably be anticipated — this obligation applies broadly, not only at specific marked locations.

Keeping the vehicle balanced through a curve means slowing down before entering it and only accelerating again once coming out of it, rather than carrying speed into the turn or shifting gears mid-curve.
Traffic law requires a motorcycle's lights to be functioning whenever it is ridden, so a rider whose low beam fails during a night drive is legally barred from continuing until it is fixed.

A new driver under 21 driving a private car may not carry more than two passengers besides himself unless accompanied by a supervising escort, a statutory restriction meant to limit distraction risk for young drivers.
The reflective traffic vest requirement in Israeli law applies to all motor vehicles, without exception for particular vehicle categories.
The vest must be kept within the driver's compartment, not stored in the trunk, so it can be put on before stepping out — except for motorcycles, which have no separate compartment to keep it in.

The duty to wear a reflective vest applies when the driver or a passenger gets out of a vehicle stopped on a non-urban road without a pavement, since visibility to oncoming traffic is especially reduced there.
A new driver convicted of exceeding the speed limit during the two-year probation period will not automatically receive a regular license once that period ends.
A new driver convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs during the probation period is barred from receiving a regular license at the end of the two-year period.
The statutory speed limit for a private minibus (falling under vehicles up to 12 tons) on a freeway, unless otherwise posted, is 110 km/h.

Driving without the mandatory escort during the new-driver probation period is a statutory violation that, like speeding or drunk driving, can prevent the driver from being granted a regular license once the two-year period ends.

Israeli law requires a motorcycle's lights to be lit at all times it is ridden, day or night, so a malfunctioning headlight — even the high beam during daytime — legally bars the rider from continuing until it's repaired.

Driving through deep water can wet the brake pads and discs and temporarily reduce their friction, so a driver should check the brakes are still working effectively afterward before resuming normal speed.
A properly worn seat belt keeps an occupant from being thrown against the vehicle's interior or ejected during a sudden stop or crash, reducing the severity of injury.
Overtaking a bus that has moved out of the traffic lane to pass another vehicle is prohibited on every type of road, since it compounds an already hazardous overtaking situation.
A driver's actual ability to control a vehicle improves when speed is matched to the changing road and traffic conditions, not simply by driving faster or relying on road conditions alone.

Headlights that are not properly aligned fail to illuminate the road ahead where it's actually needed, directly reducing the driver's visibility rather than affecting alertness or vehicle control in some other way.
Keeping the windshield clean reduces the scattering of oncoming headlight glare, which is the effective way to cut down on being dazzled at night rather than using dark glasses or a sunshade.
A narrow bridge requires slowing down both while approaching and while crossing it, since the reduced width leaves less margin for error at normal speed.

After dark both the driver's ability to see hazards and other road users' ability to see the driver are limited, which is why extra caution is required at night rather than only in specific weather conditions.

High beams may be used on an inter-urban road when traffic conditions allow and there is no vehicle ahead that the beam could dazzle, matching the legal rule on dimming lights whenever another driver could be blinded.

A panoramic (convex) mirror widens the field of view by making reflected objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are, which is why drivers are cautioned that such objects are closer than they appear.
Reverse lights are designed to switch on automatically only while the driver has the vehicle shifted into reverse gear, turning off as soon as reverse is no longer engaged.
